figures.title: National activity: annual FAI 2023, 2024, 2025
figures.communicates: Annual detected-candidate activity index per usable day relative to the frozen 2023-2025 reference.
figures.limitations: The annual mean over the matched baseline dates is 100 by construction, so 'above/below 100' is relative to a 3-year reference, not to a normal level. Differences may reflect detection, processing, cloud and static-source effects as well as real activity; no cause is implied.

figures.title: National activity: monthly FAI time series
figures.communicates: Month-to-month variation of the headline index, with the share of usable days beneath each month.
figures.limitations: Hollow markers = partial coverage; grey shading = no published value. Months with fewer usable days are less reliable. The strong seasonal pattern should not be read as causal.

figures.title: National activity: daily FAI time series
figures.communicates: Day-level variability of detected candidate activity and where daily values are not available.
figures.limitations: Daily values are noisy (small cell-day counts, overpass timing, cloud). Unusable days are drawn as gaps with red shading and are not interpolated or treated as zero. Axis is symmetric-log above 100.

figures.title: National activity: seasonal comparison
figures.communicates: How each meteorological season compares between years in the headline series.
figures.limitations: DJF 2023 is not published because its window is incomplete (Dec 2022 is outside the dataset); marked n/a, not zero. Seasons use three years only; 'seasonal' differences are descriptive.

figures.title: Geographic distribution: Egypt candidate-activity heatmap
figures.communicates: Where VIIRS vegetation-fire candidates were detected most often, on the existing 0.05° grid.
figures.limitations: Blank cells = no candidate detected in this product, not 'verified no fire'. Counts are raw cell-days on observed days (not coverage-normalised); many top cells lie near static thermal sources (see static overlay figure). Outline is schematic, not survey-grade.

figures.title: Geographic distribution: annual comparison 2023 / 2024 / 2025
figures.communicates: Whether the spatial pattern of candidate detections persisted across years, on one shared colour scale.
figures.limitations: Raw cell-days; years have different numbers of usable days and NOAA-21 only starts in March 2023, so year-to-year differences are not purely activity changes. See national figures for index-normalised values.

figures.title: Geographic distribution: active-cell frequency
figures.communicates: How often each cell had a candidate detection, as a share of national usable days.
figures.limitations: Denominator = national usable days (coverage_basis = record_presence_proxy), not cell-specific observations; high values near static thermal sources may reflect persistent non-vegetation heat.

figures.title: Geographic distribution: annual active-cell frequency
figures.communicates: Annual maps of the share of usable days with a candidate detection per cell.
figures.limitations: Same limitations as the all-years frequency map; zero-frequency cells are left blank.

figures.title: Geographic distribution: candidate activity vs static thermal sources
figures.communicates: Spatial coincidence between high candidate counts and persistent static thermal sources.
figures.limitations: Spatial coincidence is descriptive only and does not establish that candidates are caused by, or are false alarms of, static sources.

figures.title: 1° blocks: annual FAI relative to each block's own baseline
figures.communicates: For each eligible block, whether a year was above or below that block's own 2023-2025 reference (100).
figures.limitations: Colours show deviation from each block's own baseline, not activity level; blocks are neither ranked nor comparable in level. Ineligible blocks are hatched, not shown as zero.

figures.title: 1° blocks: each block against its own baseline (geographic order)
figures.communicates: Per-block yearly change relative to that block's own frozen reference; panels are in north-to-south, west-to-east order, never sorted by value.
figures.limitations: Only eligible blocks are drawn. Dashed line = the block's own baseline (100). Bars of different blocks must not be compared as activity levels.

figures.title: Sensor analysis: individual VIIRS sensor indices
figures.communicates: Each sensor is indexed on its own usable days and own baseline; close tracking indicates robustness.
figures.limitations: NOAA-21 science starts 2023-03-01 (no value Jan-Feb 2023, a gap not zero). VIIRS sensors observe the same fires; counts from different sensors are never summed as independent events. MODIS has no FAI.

figures.title: Sensor analysis: annual single-sensor indices
figures.communicates: Whether the 2023 > 2024 > 2025 pattern is consistent across sensors.
figures.limitations: Each sensor uses its own usable days and baseline; differences mix sensor characteristics and day sets.

figures.title: Sensor analysis: inter-sensor index spread
figures.communicates: How much the index changes depending on which VIIRS sensor is used.
figures.limitations: The spread is the range (max - min) of single-sensor indices computed on their own usable days and baselines. It is a descriptive sensitivity to sensor choice, NOT a confidence interval, standard error or uncertainty estimate.

figures.title: Sensor analysis: agreement between sensors
figures.communicates: How closely different sensors flag the same 0.05° cells and move together day to day.
figures.limitations: MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) are kept distinct; MODIS is compared on days when MODIS has records. Low agreement reflects different overpass times and resolution, not which sensor is 'right'. Counts from different sensors are not additive.

figures.title: Sensor analysis: monthly candidate cell-days by sensor (separate panels)
figures.communicates: Raw monthly 0.05° cell-days per sensor family on that sensor's used days, one panel each.
figures.limitations: Hatched bars = low-coverage month. Raw cell-days depend on the number of usable days and sensor resolution; panels must not be added up or compared as fire counts.

figures.title: Static thermal sources: core vs excl3x3 FAI
figures.communicates: Whether the temporal pattern survives when cells in or next to static thermal sources are removed.
figures.limitations: Static-source exclusion is a SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS, not a correction: each series has its own baseline, removing cells removes real vegetation candidates too, and it does not prove remaining detections are vegetation fires.

figures.title: Static thermal sources: exposure share
figures.communicates: How much of detected candidate activity falls in cells in or adjacent to static thermal sources.
figures.limitations: R < 1 means a higher static-neighbourhood share than in the reference. This is a diagnostic of exposure, not a correction and not evidence of cause.

figures.title: Static thermal sources: proximity and per-sensor counts
figures.communicates: A large share of candidate cell-days lies in or next to static-source cells.
figures.limitations: Descriptive association only; no causation is claimed. Static cell counts differ by sensor (MODIS vs VIIRS kept separate) and must not be summed across sensors.

figures.title: Confidence analysis: all confidence vs excluding low confidence
figures.communicates: Whether the temporal pattern depends on keeping low-confidence VIIRS detections.
figures.limitations: Each series has its own baseline, so level differences are small by design. Confidence classes are the sensor's own letter classes (n/h kept); MODIS confidence is not used. This is a sensitivity analysis only.

figures.title: Confidence analysis: low-confidence contribution
figures.communicates: How much of the detected activity rests on low-confidence classes, by month and by sensor-year.
figures.limitations: Low confidence does not mean false; high confidence does not mean confirmed fire. The share rising over years may reflect processing or environmental differences; no cause is implied.

figures.title: Data coverage: usable and unusable days (headline series)
figures.communicates: Which days entered the headline index; 28 of 1096 days were unusable and excluded.
figures.limitations: Unusable days are excluded from the index, never counted as zero activity. Usable-day status is derived from record presence, a proxy for observation coverage.

figures.title: Data coverage: observed-day share by sensor and month
figures.communicates: Which sensor-months have records on few days (red) and which are almost complete (green).
figures.limitations: MODIS has days with no records that cannot be confirmed as zero-detection days (unconfirmed gaps); NOAA-21 is expected only from 2023-03-01. Low share = incomplete observation, not low activity.

figures.title: Data coverage: gap runs by sensor
figures.communicates: Each bar is a run of consecutive days without usable records for that sensor.
figures.limitations: 'No records (unconfirmed)' means the absence could be real quiet or missing data; it is never read as zero activity. Documented source gaps are known outages.

figures.title: Data coverage: monthly quality labels
figures.communicates: Quality label and usable-day counts for each month of the headline series.
figures.limitations: Labels come from Phase 5 coverage rules (kappa = usable / expected days); partial-coverage months should be interpreted with caution.

figures.title: Seasonal patterns: month-of-year cycle for each year
figures.communicates: Which months tend to show the highest index and whether the pattern repeats across years.
figures.limitations: Three years cannot define a climatology; correlation with season is not causation.

figures.title: Daily patterns: day vs night diagnostics
figures.communicates: Whether the 2023-2025 change appears in both daytime and night-time overpasses.
figures.limitations: Day/night is the sensor's overpass flag, not a time-of-burning estimate; day and night cells overlap so the union is not the sum. Only yearly diagnostics exist, so no monthly day/night chart is made.

figures.title: Daily patterns: hourly profile of detections by sensor
figures.communicates: At which hours of the day each sensor's detections occur, separately for candidates and static sources.
figures.limitations: Hours are plotted in UTC (the original time reference), derived from the Africa/Cairo local hour and UTC offset (2 or 3) in the source file; add 2-3 h for Cairo local time. Hours reflect satellite overpass times, not when fires burn; sensors are not summed.

figures.title: Interactive spatial candidate-activity map
figures.communicates: Hover to read per-cell candidate cell-days per year and active-day frequency; toggle static cells.
figures.limitations: Same as the static spatial maps; self-contained canvas (no external libraries, plotly not available).

figures.title: Interactive monthly headline FAI
figures.communicates: Hover to read monthly FAI, quality label and usable days.
figures.limitations: Hollow markers = partial coverage; gaps for unpublished months; self-contained canvas.
